text:
sam: Heads up — ran a cross-cloud A100 int8 warmstart sweep this morning. GCP tail is weirdly higher than AWS/Azure for small batches.
jess: what numbers are we seeing?
sam: quick summary: batch=1 p95 on GCP ~2.5x AWS, but at batch=8 throughput flips and GCP ends up slightly higher. p50s are close. suspect I/O or kernel selection differences during kv-cache warm.
anita: did you pin drivers/CUDA across images?
sam: yes — AWS: driver 525.85 + CUDA 11.8; GCP: driver 535.86 + CUDA 12.1; Azure: 526.47 + CUDA 11.8. Built int8 kernels with Triton/Cutlass. CUDA12 picked a different int8 matmul kernel on GCP.
mohit: can you paste the perf command and the core excerpt?
sam: ```
# run script
PYTHONPATH=. python infra/bench/run_infer.py \
  --model redwood-7b-qint8 \
  --batch-sizes 1,8 \
  --seq-len 256 \
  --quant int8 \
  --warmup 50 \
  --steps 500 \
  --profile nvtx
```
sam: output (trimmed):
AWS p95 bs=1: 42ms, p50: 16ms
GCP p95 bs=1: 110ms, p50: 18ms
Azure p95 bs=1: 50ms, p50: 17ms
AWS thpt bs=8: 380 toks/s
GCP thpt bs=8: 420 toks/s
Azure thpt bs=8: 365 toks/s

jess: :thinking_face: p50s are similar but GCP p95 spike + huge throughput at larger bs.
sam: flamegraphs show memcpy spikes during kv cache refill on GCP right after context switch. nvprof/ncu shows more sync memcpy calls from device -> host path.
anita: could be different default copy engine or async memcpy fallback in 535 driver. Also PCIe topology matters (root complex + TLPs). What instance SKUs?
sam: AWS p4dn (NVLink+FBMEM), GCP a2-highgpu-1g (A100 but host PCIe gen3), Azure NDv5 (NVLink). So GCP looks like it's on a host with host-visible PCIe path for some copies.
ci-bot: Benchmark run uploaded: https://internal/perf/1715009999 (logs + nvprof snapshots)
mohit: try forcing older cutlass kernel selection to force the CUDA11 path: export CUTLASS_KERNEL_FORCE=legacy; rerun. Also try setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and CUDA_MEMCPY_ASYNC=0 to see diff.
sam: I tried CUTLASS_KERNEL_FORCE=legacy — p95 on GCP dropped ~20% but still ~1.8x AWS. Also observed ~0.3% token-level drift in outputs vs AWS on int8 path (rounding differences). QA caught it in a small eval set.
anj: (typo)
anita: rounding diffs are plausible if accumulation order or INT8->FP32 conv path changed. Are eval failures material?
sam: small regressions in some edge prompts — not huge but visible. We'll need to check whether it's numerical or kernel bug.
anita: proposed action items:
1) Bisect GCP driver 535.x -> 534.x to see regression point.
2) Run PCIe microbench (p2p/host-to-device bdw) across clouds to confirm gen differences.
3) Rebuild userland with CUDA11.8 on GCP container to isolate runtime vs driver.
4) Rerun with forced kernel selection and with async memcpy toggled.
mohit: I'll take (3) and (4) and try a pinned build.
sam: will run driver bisect + pcie microbench and upload results. tagging @mohit for kernel overrides.
mohit: :thumbsup:
jess: thanks — please paste short summary into the crosscloud bench doc when done so infra can plan capacity sizing accordingly.
sam: will do, dropping raw csvs into s3://redwood-perf/crosscloud/1715009999/ and linking here when finished.
